react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary enrichment paradigms converged on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA returned Tryptophan metabolism (KEGG:map00380, FDR=8.59e-19, 7/54 metabolites) as the top hit across all 15 databases, with WikiPathways WP:WP465 (FDR=4.02e-15, 6/62 metabolites) and the kynurenine-specific WP:WP4210 'Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production' (FDR=9.41e-11) immediately below. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently ranked hsa00380 at position 0 (p=5.41e-09, 6/41 metabolites hit). Mummichog's m/z-direct empirical-compound network also returned Tryptophan metabolism at rank 0 (p=0.002, 9/17 metabolites on the network), confirming the signal is robust across both annotation-based and mass-features paradigms. The serotonin/melatonin branch (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR=2.14e-08) and the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR=9.48e-09) further sub-divide the signal. Driver metabolites span three tryptophan branches: L-tryptophan itself (C00078), the neuroactive serotonergic arm via tryptamine (C00398) and indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), the kynurenine shunt via 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) and quinolinic acid (C03722), and the melatonin biosynthetic end-product (C01598). Reconciled InChIKey first-blocks confirm all eight tested compounds are structurally distinct, ruling out namespace artefacts. Second-tier Mummichog hits also implicate glycerophospholipid metabolism (acetylcholine, C01996), the pentose phosphate pathway (deoxyribose 1-phosphate, C00672), and ascorbate/dihydrolipoate metabolism (dihydrolipoate, C02147), indicating secondary perturbation of redox and nucleotide-sugar homeostasis. In a biological context, coordinated changes in tryptophan catabolites suggest treatment-driven activation of IDO-mediated tryptophan depletion, while elevated 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid signal a kynurenine-pathway shift toward neuroactive and immunomodulatory metabolites.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm pathway analysis of 12 differentially abundant metabolites identified tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected pathway across three complementary methods. RaMP ORA returned KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism as the top hit with FDR=8.59e-19, driven by seven metabolites (tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, serotonin, L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, melatonin). WikiPathways WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) ranked second with FDR=4.02e-15 (6 metabolites), while WP:WP4210 Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production ranked third with FDR=9.41e-11 (4 metabolites). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis confirmed MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top hit (p=0.0016) with 16 of 17 pathway metabolites matched. The convergence across ORA and network-based paradigms establishes robust enrichment of the tryptophan catabolic network, spanning serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis through the kynurenine branch to NAD+ biosynthesis.
